title: WPSS/1633/2019 of RAJESH KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1633 of 2019
Rajesh Kumar ... Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ... Respondents
Advocates : Mr. Shivanand Bhatt, Advocate, for the petitioner
Mr. Rakesh Kunwar, Addl. CSC, for the State of Uttarakhand
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The petitioner in the present writ petition has contended
that he is presently working with respondents, after having been
appointed as a Peon in the Government Girls Inter College,
Papey, Bageshwar. The petitioner contends, that his appointment
was made on the post of Peon on the basis of a disability
certificate, which was issued in his favour, holding thereof, that
the petitioner is a 90% disabled person.
2. The grievance of the petitioner, as modulated in the writ
petition, is to the effect that as if the respondents are not
considering the aspect of grant of 4% of reservation, which was
meant to be extended to the disabled persons under the
Government Order, which has been referred thereto in the relief
clause i.e. the Government Order dated 14th June 2018.
3. If the Government Order dated 14th June 2018, is taken
into consideration, in fact, it was not a concerted decision, which
was made for the purposes of extension of benefit on the
promotional post; rather it had laid down the parameters, that the
decision-making process was to be taken in future, as would be
apparent from the conclusion drawn from the Government Order.

2
4. Even otherwise also, if the provisions of Section 34 of the
Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 is taken into
consideration, which is extracted hereunder:-
"34. Reservation.-(1) Every appropriate Government shall
appoint in every Government establishment, not less than four per
cent. of the total number of vacancies in the cadre strength in each
group of posts meant to be filled with persons with benchmark
disabilities of which, one per cent. each shall be reserved for
persons with benchmark disabilities under clauses (a), (b) and (c)
and one per cent. for persons with benchmark disabilities under
clauses (d) and (e), namely:-
(a) blindness and low vision;
(b) deaf and hard of hearing;
(c) locomotor disability including cerebral palsy, leprosy
cured, dwarfism, acid attack victims and muscular dystrophy;
(d) autism, intellectual disability, specific learning
disability and mental illness;
(e) multiple disabilities from amongst persons under
clauses (a) to (d) including deaf-blindness in the posts identified
for each disabilities:
Provided that the reservation in promotion shall be in
accordance with such instructions as are issued by the appropriate
Government from time to time:
Provided further that the appropriate Government, in
consultation with the Chief Commissioner or the State
Commissioner, as the case may be, may, having regard to the type
of work carried out in any Government establishment, by
notification and subject to such conditions, if any, as may be
specified in such notifications exempt any Government
establishment from the provisions of this section.
(2) Where in any recruitment year any vacancy cannot be
filled up due to non-availability of a suitable person with
benchmark disability or for any other sufficient reasons, such
vacancy shall be carried forward in the succeeding recruitment
year and if in the succeeding recruitment year also suitable person
with benchmark disability is not available, it may first be filled by
interchange among the five categories and only when there is no
person with disability available for the post in that year, the
employer shall fill up the vacancy by appointment of a person,
other than a person with disability: Provided that if the nature of
vacancies in an establishment is such that a given category of
person cannot be employed, the vacancies may be interchanged
among the five categories with the prior approval of the
appropriate Government.
(3) The appropriate Government may, by notification,
provide for such relaxation of upper age limit for employment of
persons with benchmark disability, as it thinks fit.
5. The applicability of 4% of reservation to a disabled person
would only apply to the services of the State Government subject
to the fulfillment of the conditions of the first proviso to sub
Section (1) of Section 34 of the Act, which is extracted
hereunder:-

3
"Provided that the reservation in promotion shall be in accordance
with such instructions as are issued by the appropriate Government from time to
time:"
6. The extension of reservation to a disabled person under the
said proviso, would only be extended to the promotional posts
subject to the directions to be issued by the State Government,
from time to time. It is contended by the learned Addl. CSC, for
the State that the State under the first proviso to Section 31 of the
Act, had issued a Government Order No. 232(1)/XXX(2)/2018
dated 26th September 2018, whereby a horizontal reservations to
the disabled persons has been extended under the first proviso to
Section 34 of the Act.
7. Hence, the issue would be that whether in pursuance to the
said Government Order, it is not a case where the reservation to
the disabled person to the extent of 4% has not been provided, in
fact, rather it has been made applicable; but the petitioner's claim
could not be considered in view of the averments made in para 5
of the counter affidavit, filed by respondent wherein a specific
case has been taken by the respondent that the petitioner's claim
for promotion based under 4% category of reservation provided
to the disabled person under the Act was considered. But
petitioner failed to qualify the promotional exercises hence his
consideration for promotion was turned down.
8. In that eventuality, failure to succeed in a promotional
exercise after the extension of 4% reservation, the petitioner
would not be able to enable to substantiate the relief, which has
been claimed by him in the writ petition. In fact, the reservation
under the proviso to Section 34, to the State Government
employee, was extended, and the petitioner was considered for
promotion, but since he did not succeeded in the promotional
exercise, his claim was rejected, which was not a subject matter

4
of challenge in the present writ petition or in any other
proceedings, after having being declared to be unsuccessful in
the promotional exercise.
9. Thus the writ petition, for the relief claimed therein is not
sustainable and the same is accordingly rejected.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
15.12.2021 Mahinder/
